entry: Political and cultural history of the [[Malay Peninsula]] and [[Borneo]], now the federation of [[Malaysia]]. Human occupation extends back at least 1.83 million years. Hinduism and Buddhism dominated early regional history under the Sumatra-based [[Srivijaya]] civilization, which peaked from the 7th to the 13th centuries. [[Islam]] took firm root in the 15th century, creating the [[Malacca Sultanate|Sultanate of Malacca]]. The Portuguese captured Malacca in 1511, and the Dutch did so in 1641 with the aid of Johor. Malayan independence came on August 31, 1957. The Federation of Malaysia formed on September 16, 1963, but [[Singapore]] was expelled in August 1965. A racial riot in 1969 led to emergency rule and the New Economic Policy of 1971. Rapid growth and urbanization followed under [[Mahathir Mohamad]] from the 1980s. The 1MDB scandal significantly influenced the 2018 general election, which brought the first change of ruling party since independence.

Civilizations of the region between the [[Tigris]] and [[Euphrates]], from Paleolithic occupation to late antiquity. The history is pieced together from archaeological excavations and, after writing appeared in the late 4th millennium BC, from written sources. Mesopotamia is often called a [[Cradle of civilization|cradle of civilization]], having been home to many of the oldest major civilizations, which enter history from the Early Bronze Age. The name, meaning land between the rivers, refers to the territory between the Euphrates and Tigris and is first attested in the 4th century BC. Sumerian city-states such as [[Uruk]] and [[Ur]] emerged in the south by about 3500 BC. In modern usage the term usually covers the period until the Arab Muslim conquests of the 7th century AD. Chronologies for the third and second millennia BC remain debated, with proposed schemes varying by as much as 150 years.

Political and cultural development of Mexico, from the first settlers more than 13,000 years ago to the present. Central and southern Mexico, known as [[Mesoamerica]], saw the rise and fall of civilizations such as the Olmecs, Mayas and [[Aztec Empire|Aztecs]]. Mesoamerican peoples developed glyph-based writing systems. After the Spanish conquest of the Aztec Empire in the 16th century, which included the fall of [[Tenochtitlan]] in 1521, the territory became [[New Spain]] and [[Christianity]] was introduced. Mexico gained independence from Spain in 1821 but faced conflicts between caudillos, the [[Mexican–American War]] and a French invasion. The [[Mexican Revolution]] led to the rise of the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI). Nationalization, reforms and development projects produced the Mexican miracle of the 1940s to 1970s. Since joining the North American Free Trade Agreement in 1994, Mexico has also faced the peso crisis and the [[Mexican drug war]].

Political and cultural development of present-day Morocco, from early hominin activity to the Alawi dynasty. Hominins were active at Thomas Quarry I in [[Casablanca]] about 1.3 million years ago. [[Phoenicia|Phoenician]] traders colonized the coast between the 8th and 6th centuries BCE, and [[Carthage]] later extended its hegemony over the coastal areas. Indigenous [[Berbers|Berber]] monarchs ruled from the 3rd century BCE until 40 CE, when the territory was annexed to the [[Roman Empire]]. Vandals overran it in the mid-5th century CE, and the [[Byzantine Empire]] recovered it in the 6th century. Muslims conquered the region in the early 8th century, but it broke away from the [[Umayyad Caliphate]] after the Berber Revolt of 740. The Idrisid dynasty established the Moroccan state about half a century later, followed by the [[Almoravid dynasty|Almoravid]], Almohad, Marinid and Wattasid dynasties. The Alawi dynasty has ruled Morocco since the 17th century and remains the reigning dynasty.

Political and cultural development of present-day Myanmar, from prehistoric settlement to the present. The Pyu city-states, founded by Tibeto-Burman speakers, adopted [[Theravada]] Buddhism. The Bamar people entered the upper Irrawaddy valley in the early 9th century and founded the [[Pagan Kingdom]] (1044–1297), the first unification of the valley. After the Mongol invasion of 1287, several rival kingdoms competed. The [[Toungoo dynasty]] (1510–1752) reunified the country and briefly ruled the largest empire in Southeast Asian history. The [[Konbaung dynasty]] restored the kingdom in the 18th century, but the Anglo-Burmese wars (1824–85) led to British colonial rule. Independence came on January 4, 1948, and one of the longest-running civil wars followed. The military ruled in various forms from 1962 to 2010, and again from 2021, when it overturned the government of [[Aung San Suu Kyi]]. Myanmar has become one of the least developed nations in the world.

Political and social development of Nigeria, from early settlement to the present democratic republic. The [[Nok culture]] began around 1500 BC, followed by ancient civilizations such as the Ife Empire, the [[Benin|Benin Kingdom]] and the [[Oyo Empire]]. Islam reached the region through the Bornu Empire and Hausa kingdoms in the 11th century. After 1804, Usman dan Fodio unified a large territory in a jihad, creating the [[Sokoto Caliphate]]. Coastal towns took part in the [[Atlantic slave trade|transatlantic slave trade]], and British expansion began from [[Lagos]]. Great Britain controlled almost all of present-day Nigeria from 1903, and the territory was united under a single administration in 1914. Nigeria gained independence in 1960, and the Biafran War of 1967 to 1970 became one of the worst humanitarian disasters of the late twentieth century. The country transitioned to a democratic federal republic in 1999. The [[Boko Haram]] insurgency drew international attention around 2014.

Political and cultural history of the strip of northern Africa between the [[Sahara]] and the Mediterranean Sea. The earliest known humans lived in the region around 260,000 BC. Green Sahara conditions, with lakes and savanna, ended between 5500 and 4000 BP. In the 1st millennium AD, the Sahara became a major trade zone for camel caravans. The Nile Valley gave rise to [[Ancient Egypt|ancient Egypt]], one of the world's first civilizations. The [[Phoenicia|Phoenician]]-founded city of [[Carthage]] challenged Rome in the [[Punic Wars]]. Arab Muslim conquests from the 7th century brought Islamization and Arabic dominance, and the Berber-led Almoravids and Almohads later ruled. France invaded Algeria in 1830, beginning systematic colonization, and most states gained independence after World War II. Oil wealth in Libya and Algeria fueled development but also corruption. Popular uprisings, including the [[Arab Spring]] of 2011, followed.

Human occupation of Oceania, including [[Australia]], New Zealand and the Pacific island nations. Settlement of the region began about 70,000 years ago in Near Oceania and about 3,000 years ago in Remote Oceania. Indigenous Australians are thought to have arrived about 50,000 years ago, although estimates reach back to 125,000 years ago. The earliest definite human remains, those of Mungo Man, date to about 40,000 years ago. Settlers reached New Guinea and the nearby islands between 50,000 and 30,000 years ago. The [[Austronesian peoples|Austronesian-speaking]] Lapita peoples spread through Remote Oceania from about 3,500 years ago, bringing pottery and crops such as taro. A 2008 genetic study found that [[Polynesia|Polynesians]] and Micronesians have little genetic relation to [[Melanesia|Melanesians]] but are closely related to East Asians. European contact began in the 16th century, and [[James Cook]] charted the Pacific from 1769 to 1779. Colonization followed in the 19th century.

Pre-independence history of the region that is now Pakistan, shared with neighboring Afghanistan, India, Iran and Tibet. Neolithic farming at Mehrgarh in Balochistan dates to 7000–5500 BCE. The [[Indus Valley Civilisation]], one of three early civilizations of the Old World, flourished from about 3300 BCE in the basin of the [[Indus River]], with major sites at Mohenjo-daro and Harappa. Successive empires, including the Achaemenid, Maurya and Kushan, left their mark. After the Islamic conquest, the region was ruled by the Umayyad, Ghaznavid and Ghurid dynasties, the [[Delhi Sultanate]] and the [[Mughal Empire]]. The [[East India Company]] gained control in the first half of the 19th century, and the British Raj ruled directly after 1858. The Pakistan Movement, led by [[Muhammad Ali Jinnah]], ended with the [[Partition of India|partition of British India]] and Pakistan's independence on August 14, 1947.

Political and cultural development of Peru, from the first civilizations of the coast and Andes to the republic. The Norte Chico civilization, centered on Caral, was the oldest in the Americas, and its city dates to about 2500 BC. When the Spanish arrived in the 16th century, the highlands of southern Peru were the center of the [[Inca Empire]], the largest and most advanced state in pre-Columbian America. After the conquest of the Incas, led by [[Francisco Pizarro]] in 1532, the [[Spanish Empire|Spanish]] established a viceroyalty over most of their South American domains. Peru declared independence in 1821, but the Battle of Ayacucho in 1824 secured it. In the War of the Pacific (1879–1884), Chile seized Peru's nitrate-rich southern provinces. Cycles of military dictatorship and populist government followed, along with the Maoist Shining Path insurgency. Neoliberal reforms under [[Alberto Fujimori]] in the early 1990s stabilized the economy.

Political development of the Polish state, from Piast rule in the 10th century to the Third Polish Republic. Duke [[Mieszko I]] adopted Western Christianity in 966, and [[Bolesław I the Brave]] formally reconstituted the realm as a kingdom in 1025. Close ties with [[Lithuania]] under the Jagiellonian dynasty led to the [[Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth]] in 1569, one of Europe's great powers. Its elective monarchy and noble democracy declined from the mid-17th century, and the Commonwealth ended in 1795 after partitions by Russia, Prussia and Austria. Poland regained independence in 1918 as the Second Polish Republic. [[Nazi Germany]] and the [[Soviet Union]] invaded in 1939, starting [[World War II]], and millions of Polish citizens died under occupation. After 1945 a communist state was established, and the Solidarity movement helped bring about a peaceful transition to democracy. The Third Polish Republic was founded in 1989.

Political development of Portugal, from the Roman conquest to membership in the [[European Union]]. The Roman conquest of the Iberian Peninsula established the provinces of Lusitania and Gallaecia, and Germanic tribes, including the [[Visigothic Kingdom]] in the south, later controlled the territory. The [[Umayyad Caliphate]] conquered the Visigoth kingdom in 711–716 and founded [[Al-Andalus]]. Portugal broke away from the Kingdom of Galicia in 1095, and Afonso Henriques proclaimed himself king in 1139. The Treaty of Windsor with England in 1386 is the longest-lasting diplomatic treaty in recorded history. During the [[Age of Discovery]], Portugal became a world power, but a dynastic union with [[Spain]] lasted from 1580 until the Portuguese Restoration War began in 1640. Its largest colony, Brazil, was lost in 1822. A 1926 coup installed a dictatorship that lasted until 1974. Portugal is a founding member of [[NATO]] and joined the European Economic Community in 1986, now the European Union.

Political development of the East Slavic lands that became Russia, from [[Kievan Rus']] to the Russian Federation. The state of Rus' was established in 862 and adopted Christianity from the [[Byzantine Empire]] in 988. Mongol invasions in 1237–1240 ended its unity. The Grand Duchy of Moscow gathered surrounding principalities, and [[Ivan the Terrible]] transformed it into the Tsardom of Russia in 1547. [[Peter the Great]] renamed the state the Russian Empire in 1721 and founded St. Petersburg, and [[Catherine the Great]] took power in 1762. The Russian Revolution of 1917 led to the October Revolution, and the Soviet Union was formed in 1922. After World War II it became a superpower in the [[Cold War]]. [[Mikhail Gorbachev]]'s reforms led to the dissolution of the Soviet Union, and the Russian Federation became its primary successor state. Under [[Vladimir Putin]], Russia regained global status, but its 2014 annexation of Crimea brought sanctions that were significantly expanded after its 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

Political development of the territory of Saudi Arabia, from the rise of the Al Saud dynasty in 1727 to the present. The Islamic prophet [[Muhammad]] united Arabia in the early 7th century. The modern kingdom was founded in 1932 by [[Ibn Saud|Abdulaziz bin Abdul Rahman]], who began his conquests in 1902 with the capture of [[Riyadh]] and united four historical regions. Petroleum was discovered on March 3, 1938, and Saudi Arabia became the world's second-largest oil producer and the world's largest oil exporter. Faisal's rule from 1964 to 1975 brought oil-fueled modernization, and the [[1973 oil crisis]] increased the country's political significance. In 1979, Islamist extremists briefly seized the Grand Mosque in Mecca. Under Fahd, the kingdom allied with the United States in the 1991 [[Gulf War]]. Salman became king in 2015, and his son [[Mohammed bin Salman]] effectively controls the government. He has pursued legal and social reforms and is seeking to diversify the economy through Saudi Vision 2030.

Northern European region of Denmark, Norway and Sweden, sometimes including Finland and Iceland. Ice covered almost all of Scandinavia during the last glaciation, and permanent though nomadic habitation began around 12,000 BCE. Hunter-gatherers followed the herds and salmon runs, and by the 6th millennium BC temperate forests covered southern Scandinavia. Little evidence of the [[Stone Age]], [[Bronze Age]] or [[Iron Age]] survives beyond tools, jewelry and burial cairns, although petroglyphs are widespread. The [[Viking Age]] (c. 793–1066 CE) saw Scandinavians raid and trade across Europe. The Kalmar Union (1397–1523) united the three realms under Danish hegemony, but it dissolved amid internal revolts. Sweden became a Baltic great power during the [[Thirty Years' War]]. Norway gained independence from Denmark in 1814 and from Sweden in 1905. Neutrality policies during the world wars were followed by postwar social democratic welfare states.

Political development of South Africa, from early human habitation to the post-apartheid era. Modern humans are believed to have lived in the region more than 100,000 years ago, and Bantu-speaking groups arrived from about 400 AD. The [[Dutch East India Company]] established a trading post in [[Cape Town]] under Jan van Riebeeck in April 1652. British forces invaded the Cape Colony in 1795 and 1806, and Boer settlers trekked inland during the Great Trek to found republics. Diamond and gold discoveries in the 19th century drove industrialization and led to war between the Boers and the [[British Empire]]. The Union of South Africa was created on May 31, 1910. From 1948, [[Apartheid|apartheid]], a system of racial segregation, was introduced under Afrikaner nationalism. In 1990, F. W. de Klerk unbanned the [[African National Congress]] and freed [[Nelson Mandela]], and the ANC won the first democratic election in 1994. In 2024, the ANC lost its parliamentary majority for the first time.

Mainland and maritime sub-regions of Southeast Asia, from prehistory to the present. Homo sapiens reached mainland Southeast Asia about 70,000 years ago and the islands at least 50,000 years ago. Millet and wet-rice cultivation emerged around 1700 BCE, and by about 500 BCE the Dong Son culture had developed sophisticated bronze production. The first agrarian kingdoms, such as Funan on the lower [[Mekong]], emerged around the same time. From the early centuries of the common era, most trading polities adopted Indian Hindu elements of statecraft and religion. In mainland Southeast Asia, [[Buddhism]] began to affect political structures from the 8th to 9th centuries, and [[Islam|Islamic]] ideas arrived in the islands as early as the 8th century. European colonialism and the [[Cold War]] revealed the limited political significance of most Southeast Asian polities. Most modern states enjoy self-determination and cooperate within [[ASEAN]], founded in 1967.

Political development of Spain, from Roman Hispania to the constitutional monarchy. The Romans called the peninsula Hispania, and Germanic kingdoms followed the end of Roman rule in the 5th century. The Umayyad conquest of 711 began centuries of Muslim-led rule known as [[Al-Andalus]], and the [[Reconquista]] gradually reclaimed the peninsula for Christian kingdoms. The joint rule of Isabella I and Ferdinand II, begun with their 1469 marriage, is considered the foundation of a unified Spain. Under Philip II, the Spanish Golden Age flourished. The War of the Spanish Succession brought the Bourbon dynasty to the throne in the early 18th century. Napoleonic France made Spain a puppet state, and most of its American territory was lost in the 1820s. The [[Spanish Civil War]] ended with the Nationalist victory of [[Francisco Franco]], whose fascist dictatorship lasted almost four decades. Monarchy returned under [[Juan Carlos I]], and Spain joined the [[European Union]] in 1986 and the Eurozone in 1998.

Political development of the territory of present-day Sudan and [[South Sudan]], from ancient Kush to the present. The [[Kingdom of Kush]] was allied with ancient Egypt, and its rulers conquered Egypt around 750 BC to establish the 25th dynasty. Three Christian Nubian kingdoms were established in the 6th century, and Islam spread into the Nile Valley in the 14th and 15th centuries. The [[Funj Sultanate]] dominated the region from the 16th to the 19th centuries. [[Muhammad Ali of Egypt]] seized the north and south in the 1820s, and his rule provoked the revolt that founded the [[Muhammad Ahmad|Mahdist]] State in 1881. Sudan gained independence on January 1, 1956, but it inherited north-south divisions. A civil war from 1955 to 1972 and a second from 1983 to 2005 caused about two million deaths before South Sudan seceded in 2011. The [[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|civil war that began in 2023]] continues.

Southeast Asian kingdom and state of Thailand, from Bronze Age settlement to the present. Tai-speaking peoples migrated from southern China between the 8th and 10th centuries. King [[Ramkhamhaeng]] created the Thai script in 1283. In 1351, the [[Ayutthaya Kingdom]] was founded near the Chao Phraya River. Burmese forces sacked Ayutthaya in 1767, and the Chakri dynasty founded the Rattanakosin Kingdom in [[Bangkok]] in 1782. King [[Chulalongkorn]] pursued centralizing reforms, and Thailand remained independent during European colonization. The 1932 revolution ended [[Absolute monarchy|absolute monarchy]] and established a constitutional framework. The country was renamed Thailand in 1939. After the Japanese invasion of 1941, Thailand joined the Axis. Thailand was a founding member of [[ASEAN]] in 1967. During the 70-year reign of King [[Bhumibol Adulyadej]], the country had 10 military coups and 17 constitutions.

Region of present-day Turkey, comprising [[Anatolia]] and Eastern Thrace, from prehistory to the republic. Göbekli Tepe, close to 12,000 years old, and [[Çatalhöyük]] are among the oldest Neolithic sites known. The [[Hittites|Hittite]] kingdom, centered on Hattusa, flourished in central Anatolia from about 1700 to 1200 BC. Anatolia came under [[Roman Empire|Roman]] control in the 2nd century BC. [[Seljuk Empire|Seljuk]] Turkic incursions from the 11th century led to widespread Turkic settlement and Islamization. The [[Ottoman Empire]] grew from a dynasty founded around 1299 by Osman I, and under [[Suleiman the Magnificent]] in the 16th century it spanned three continents. Ottoman defeat in World War I led to partition. The Turkish War of Independence (1919–1923), led by Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, secured sovereignty under the Treaty of Lausanne. The Republic of Türkiye was proclaimed on October 29, 1923, with Atatürk as president. The sultanate and caliphate were abolished, and the Latin script was adopted.

Political and cultural development of Vietnam, from Paleolithic settlement to reunification and the Đổi Mới reforms. The Đông Sơn culture emerged in the first millennium BCE, based on rice cultivation. After the Han conquest of [[Nanyue]] in 111 BCE, much of Vietnam was under Chinese dominance for about a thousand years. Independence was regained when the Ngô dynasty was established in 939, and a succession of local dynasties followed. France conquered the country in the 19th century, and it was integrated into [[French Indochina]] in 1887. After the Second World War and Japanese occupation, a communist insurgency led by [[Ho Chi Minh]] challenged French rule. The country was divided into two states after the French defeat. The [[Vietnam War]] ended with the [[Fall of Saigon|fall of Saigon]] in 1975, and the country was reunified under communist government in 1976. Vietnam launched the Đổi Mới reforms in 1986 and normalized relations with the [[United States]] in 1995.

Development of the research field now widely called artificial intelligence, from ancient myths to large language models. Myths of artificial beings endowed with intelligence date to antiquity. The field was founded at a 1956 workshop at [[Dartmouth College]], where the Logic Theorist program was presented. Many attendees predicted human-level machines within a generation, but progress slowed and funding dried up during periods known as AI winters. [[Deep learning]] and the transformer architecture, introduced in 2017, enabled [[Generative AI|generative AI]] and [[Large language model|large language models]] such as [[ChatGPT]].

Development of human efforts to understand the universe beyond Earth's atmosphere, from prehistoric observation to modern cosmology. Astronomy is one of the oldest natural sciences and grew from calendrical and religious practices. The Warren Field monument in Scotland, a lunar calendar created around 8,000 BC, is considered the oldest known [[Calendar|calendar]]. [[Babylonia|Babylonian]] astronomers recorded planetary positions and eclipses on clay tablets. [[Hipparchus]] compiled a star catalog around 150 BC, and [[Ptolemy]] formalized a geocentric model in the *Almagest* about 140 AD. In 1543, [[Nicolaus Copernicus]] proposed a heliocentric model, starting the Copernican Revolution. [[Johannes Kepler]] described elliptical planetary orbits, and [[Isaac Newton]] unified gravity as the force behind celestial and terrestrial motion. Later advances included the telescope, spectroscopy, and the [[Cosmic microwave background|cosmic microwave background]], which affirms Big Bang cosmology.

Development of disbelief in deities, from ancient Greek and Indian philosophy to modern [[Secularism|secularism]]. Philosophical atheist thought appeared in Europe and Asia in the 6th or 5th century BCE. In ancient [[Ancient Greece|Greece]], playwrights expressed doubt about the gods, and the atomists Leucippus and [[Democritus]] explained the world through moving [[Atom|atoms]] in the 5th century BCE. In India, the materialist Charvaka school rejected Vedic authority, and the Samkhya school, one of the [[Hinduism|Hindu]] schools, did not accept a creator deity. [[Buddhism]] and [[Jainism]] likewise did not center on deities. The term atheist was used in the 16th century, and atheism appeared in English around 1587. The Enlightenment fueled skepticism and secularism against religion in Europe.
